sections.html:
Acadiana's biggest hub, Lafayette, is where Lafayette Parish keeps its government, along the Vermilion River. In 2020 the city held 121,374 people, the consolidated city-parish 241,753 (up from 221,578 in 2010) and the metro area 478,384. New Orleans is 135 miles away, Baton Rouge 59 and Lake Charles 75. Broussard, Carencro, Scott, Youngsville and Duson are smaller municipalities inside the parish.

Energy, health care, education, technology and retail all employ local buyers. The University of Louisiana at Lafayette enrolls over 18,000 students. Oil and gas work moves with crude prices, which can push a household into a quick sale. Interstates 10 and 49 and U.S. highways 90 and 167 make commuting simple. Homes close to downtown can be quite old, and age brings repair lists.

sections.h2: Is flooding a concern for a Lafayette house?
sections.html:
The city rests on higher ground than much of south Louisiana, so serious flooding is mostly local flash flooding. Still, no lot is automatically safe. Development spans both banks of the Vermilion, and several coulees, Isaac Verot Coulee and Coulee des Poches among them, drain into it. Insurers and buyers check flood zones, so find your address on the map before listing and write down any past water.

Rain falls all year, most heavily in summer. Heat and moisture wear out cooling systems, roofs and attic vents, and a hard freeze can crack pipes. The age of the air conditioner and roof will come up with buyers.

The Lafayette Parish Assessor sets values, while bodies like the city-parish and the school board set rates. Every property must be reassessed at least once in four years, and values can still move yearly with sales.

Homestead protects the first $7,500 of assessed value (worth $75,000 of market value) on the owner's residence. A pool, outdoor kitchen, pool house or storage building owned by the same person is included. A second house or commercial building on the lot is not.

ProgramLafayette Parish detail
Homestead exemption$7,500 of assessed value, continuing while the owner lives there
Assessed value freezeAge 65 or older, permanently disabled, or a disabled veteran rated 50% or more; adjusted gross income of $100,000 or less
When the freeze endsOn sale, as of the last day of December of the year before the sale year

A freeze locks the assessed value only. Millage can still change, so the tax bill is not locked.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Lafayette assessment, and when is tax due?
sections.html:
Begin with a deputy assessor and show evidence that the value exceeds the market. Unresolved? Next comes the Lafayette Consolidated Council, which hears appeals in September, then the Louisiana Tax Commission, then district court within thirty days.

Each year's property tax is due December 31 and goes delinquent the day after. Selling late in the year? Make certain the bill is paid or settled at the closing table.

R.S. 9:3198 has Lafayette sellers complete the state property disclosure form and deliver it no later than the buyer's offer. Unknown items can be marked unknown. The form gives no warranty, and liability does not attach to an honest mistake or to passing along a report from a public body or professional you reasonably trusted. If it reaches the buyer late, the buyer gets 72 hours to withdraw, weekends and holidays not counted. Given the water and heat issues above, fill in the roof, plumbing, air conditioning and any water history with care.

A cash buyer does not rely on a lender, so there is no loan approval and no lender appraisal to wait for. Many cash buyers take a house as-is, which can spare you the repairs a financed buyer would demand after an inspection. You also avoid weeks of showings and the risk of a contract falling apart over financing. The trade-off is a lower price than a polished listing might reach, so weigh that gap against repair costs, carrying costs and your timeline.

In Lafayette this fits several common situations: an inherited house that nobody wants to maintain, a landlord with a damaged rental, an owner relocating for work, or a house with an old roof or a cooling system near the end of its life. Taxes, any mortgage and recording costs are still paid from proceeds at closing, and the notary or attorney handles the paperwork the same way as in any other sale.

A Property Maintenance Code, enforced by the Compliance Division of Lafayette Consolidated Government, covers the city and the unincorporated parish. Its Code Enforcement Section handles tall grass, litter, debris, junked items and similar nuisances, and unsafe structures are regulated through the building code.

A vacant inherited house can draw a notice when grass grows or debris builds. Clear the lot, or disclose the notice to a cash buyer so it is settled at closing. For a damaged house, ask the city-parish which rules apply.

sections.h2: How a Lafayette sale gets to closing
sections.html:
Once you say yes to an offer, the title search is ordered by a notary or attorney and your lender sends a payoff figure. Keep your deed, newest tax bill, survey and repair records at hand. Financing brings an appraisal and inspection into the schedule, but cash buyers can often close as soon as the title is clear. At signing, taxes, your loan balance and recording costs are subtracted from your proceeds, so get the settlement statement early and ask about any odd line.

Have an assessed value freeze? It ends when you sell. A listing is best for a house in good shape that can wait for financing, while a cash sale fits a house needing work or an owner against a deadline.

Gather these before you meet anyone: the deed, the survey, the last tax bill, insurance and repair records, any flood zone paperwork and the name of your mortgage servicer. If the house is inherited, add whatever shows who may sign. Lafayette buyers who commute across the parish also ask about the age of the roof and cooling system, so have those dates ready.

When comparing offers, subtract the payoff, taxes and closing costs from each so you see what you would actually receive. A higher listing price can shrink once repairs, concessions and months of carrying costs come out. A lower cash offer can look better after those same items are counted, particularly when the house needs a roof, drainage work or cleanup. Ask each buyer to put the closing date and any conditions in writing before you commit.

faqs.q: Is Lafayette a city or a parish?
faqs.a: It is both. Since 1996 the city and parish have operated as one consolidated government, the Lafayette Consolidated Government, though five other municipalities keep their own governments.

faqs.q: What does the Lafayette homestead exemption cover?
faqs.a: The first $7,500 of assessed value, equal to $75,000 of market value, on the owner's residence. A second house or commercial building on the same land is excluded.

faqs.q: Does the assessed value freeze pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. It ends on sale, as of the last day of December of the year before the sale year, and the buyer's home is assessed at current value.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Lafayette assessment?
faqs.a: Talk to a deputy assessor with evidence in hand. Next steps are the Lafayette Consolidated Council in September and then the Louisiana Tax Commission.

faqs.q: Who enforces tall grass and debris rules?
faqs.a: The Code Enforcement Section of Lafayette Consolidated Government handles tall grass, litter, junked items and similar nuisances.
